new_entities.name: Topical salicylic acid
new_entities.description: Topical salicylic-acid-containing acne treatments, including peels and leave-on products.

new_entities.name: Clinical mild acne
new_entities.description: Clinically assessed mild acne vulgaris, including inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesion burden.

edges.effect_quant: The Cochrane-derived review found little or no difference when salicylic acid was compared with tretinoin for participant-rated acne improvement, with a pooled relative risk of 1.00 (95% CI 0.92 to 1.09). Smaller peel studies still show lesion-count improvement from baseline, so the signal is positive but not dramatic.
edges.population: adolescents and adults with mild acne or mild-to-moderate acne treated with topical salicylic-acid products or peels
edges.mechanism: Salicylic acid is lipophilic and comedolytic, helping to reduce follicular plugging while providing mild anti-inflammatory activity that can improve both inflammatory and non-inflammatory lesions.
edges.summary: Topical salicylic acid helps mild acne, but the literature does not support calling it a superstar monotherapy. It works best as a useful, usually tolerable comedolytic option rather than a clearly superior treatment.
edges.caveats: Much of the evidence comes from peels, small comparative trials, or heterogeneous topical regimens. This edge is intentionally boring because the signal is helpful but modest.

evidence.citation: LiuH et al 2020 J Evid Based Med
evidence.notes: Evidence-based topical treatments (azelaic acid, salicylic acid, nicotinamide, sulfur, zinc, and fruit acid) for acne: an abridged version of a Cochrane systematic review.
